title: Stateless request batching proxy - draft
content:
Purpose
------
Quick brain-dump for a lightweight stateless HTTP proxy that performs request-side batching for many small inference calls. Goal: a compact, horizontally-scalable fronting layer that can aggregate tiny requests into efficient tokens-per-GPU batches without requiring session affinity or client-side session management. Target use-cases: webhook-style inference (short prompts, high QPS), mobile clients doing 1-2 turn calls, embedding micro-batches from many callers.

Principles
- Stateless between requests: no server-side per-conversation state kept in the proxy. Allows easy autoscaling and simple health checks.
- Short aggregation windows: prefer latency-bound batching (e.g. 10-30ms range configurable) over long waits.
- Idempotency and dedupe: clients supply idempotency keys for retry safety; proxy attempts dedupe in-flight duplicates within the same batch window.
- Tenant-aware but not tenant-pinned: proxy knows tenant id to apply quotas but does not hold long-lived per-tenant memory.

API shape (sketch)
POST /v1/proxy/batch
Headers:
- Authorization: Bearer <token>
- X-Tenant-Id: <tenant-id>
- X-Idempotency-Key: <opt>
- X-Client-Timeout-Ms: <opt override>
Body (JSON):
{
  "requests": [
    { "req_id": "uuid-1", "model": "redwood-3b", "input": "Summarize: ...", "max_tokens": 64, "top_p": 0.95 },
    { "req_id": "uuid-2", "model": "redwood-3b", "input": "Answer: ...", "max_tokens": 16 }
  ]
}
Response (success):
{
  "batch_id": "batch-20250103-0001",
  "responses": [
    { "req_id": "uuid-1", "status": "ok", "output": "...", "latency_ms": 82 },
    { "req_id": "uuid-2", "status": "ok", "output": "...", "latency_ms": 82 }
  ]
}
Partial/failure semantics:
- Per-request status inside responses. Proxy returns 207-multi-status equivalent but we'll use 200 with per-item statuses for simplicity.
- Retries: if idempotency key provided, proxy guarantees at-most-once forwarding within a short TTL (configurable, e.g. 30s) using an in-memory recent-keys LRU. Because layer is stateless across instances, dedupe only works per-instance (acceptable tradeoff).

Batching heuristics and config
- Window ms: default 20ms (configurable per-route/tenant).
- Max batch size: 128 requests or configurable by model family.
- Soft token limit: estimate tokens per request and stop adding once estimated token-count exceeds threshold for efficient GPU kernels.
- Tenant isolation: if tenant has high QPS, avoid letting a single tenant consume entire batch; enforce per-tenant-request cap per-batch (default 16).
- Backpressure: proxy tracks queue depth and exposes X-Proxy-Queue-Length in responses for observability; when queue depth > threshold, respond 429 or fast-fail depending on client hint header X-Prefer-Fast-Fail.

Runtime diagram (ASCII)
client -> proxy instance N (http) -> local in-flight batch builder -> kernel-scheduler -> model-pool (rpc to serving-runtime) -> responses -> proxy maps outputs to original req_id -> client

Notes: kernel-scheduler groups compatible requests (same model variant, same sampling params) before sending to model-pool to avoid compilation cost. Compatibility check is cheap (bitmask of parametrized fields).

Telemetry / events
- batch.created (batch_id, tenant, size, est_tokens, window_ms)
- batch.sent_to_runtime (batch_id, backend_latency_ms)
- batch.item.resp (req_id, status, latency_ms)
- proxy.queue.sample (queue_len)
- dedupe.hit/miss (idempotency-key)
All emitted to central ingest with tenant tags.

Operational considerations
- Healthcheck must include recent successful roundtrip to serving pool for config correctness test. But keep health probe low overhead (single no-op request).
- Rolling restart: because proxy is stateless it's safe, only caveat is dedupe LRU is lost; acceptable. Documented in runbook.
- VM/container sizing: CPU-bound for small inputs (many inflight JSON parses), so use modest vCPU, enable HTTP keepalives, and tune net thread pools.

Edge cases & open questions
- Idempotency across instances: should we provide an optional Redis-backed dedupe layer for enterprise tenants who need cross-instance at-most-once guarantees? Pros: stronger semantics; Cons: extra latency and operational complexity.
- Streaming responses: current model assumes non-streaming batched calls. Adding streaming requires mapping token streams back to request boundaries — doable but more complex (probably a separate flow).
- Cost attribution: when a batch contains mixed tenants, runtime cost split becomes fuzzy. Suggest attribute by estimated token share. Need alignment with billing.
- Large single requests: if a single request is huge (long context), we should bypass batching and route directly to a dedicated path (configurable).

Tests / validation plan
- Synthetic load test: many small requests from 1000 tenants, measure tail-latency at P99 and P999, compare with unbatched baseline.
- Dedupe correctness: simulate duplicate in-flight retries with same idempotency key and confirm one effective forward.
- Failure injection: drop backend responses, ensure proxy returns per-item error and not hang.

Rollout strategy
- Canary small subset of traffic (dev tier) with aggressive telemetry and 2x sampling rate. Gradually enable for more tenants, expose config knobs in console.

Next steps / TODOs
- [ ] spike: implement PoC in Go using single worker loop and channel-based batch builder (2-3d).
- [ ] benchmark: measure CPU and latency with 1-4k rps of 1-3 token inputs.
- [ ] design doc: formalize compatibility bitmask and kernel grouping logic.
- [ ] discuss dedupe persistence option with infra/enterprise.

Random scribbles
- If we want zero affinity, careful about caching tokens/KV — we can't rely on cache across proxy instances. Any cross-request KV caching needs runtime support.
- Could expose an opt-in header X-Allow-Batch-Bumping: prefer to add small cheap filler tokens to align lengths for kernel throughput (controversial).

References / related
- GH PR: runtime/pull/482 (batching kernel api)
- Infra: JIRA-ENG-1294 (proxy scaling)
- CL notes: convo with SRE about queue probes (slack thread #ingress-batching)

End of scratchpad.
